source.author: Neel Somani
source.background: Former Citadel quantitative researcher, power & gas
source.title: Power 2026 — Electricity Pricing in the Age of AI

chapters.title: Preface: Motivation
chapters.key: AI demand exploding; power is the real constraint; DC ~5% of US consumption; demand doubling every 2 years

chapters.title: Fundamentals of Commodities Pricing
chapters.key: System balance equation; marginal pricing; ISOs; power is special (grid frequency, ISO dispatch)

chapters.title: The Power Plant
chapters.key: EIA-860; merit order; heat rates; SCGT vs CCGT vs peaker; offer curves; startup costs

chapters.title: To Build A Power Plant
chapters.key: Scoping, site selection, financing, construction, operation; BTM compute; PPAs; HRCOs; EPC; turbine backlog

chapters.title: Case Study: Homer City
chapters.key: 2 GW coal → 4.4 GW gas; PJM; $10B cost; ~6 heat rate; EQT partner; PA DEP air permit Nov 2025; 1000 workers

chapters.title: Meeting the Growing Demand
chapters.key: Gov responses; separate grids; propensity to buy; Anthropic/TeraWulf $19B 400MW 20yr; SpaceX/Reflection ~$5000/MWh

chapters.title: Power Markets in the United States
chapters.key: PJM (most liquid, VA data center capital); MISO (coal retirements, wind); CAISO (NP-15/SP-15, renewables, no coal); ERCOT (isolated, energy-only, $9000 spikes, negative wind); SPP; NYISO; ISO-NE

chapters.title: Case Study: Alberta
chapters.key: Energy-only market; scarcity rent; C$1000 cap; duck curve; batteries flatten curve; AECO gas hub; aggressive restructuring

chapters.title: The Production Cost Model
chapters.key: Minimize total system cost; LMP = Lagrange multiplier of balance constraint; DA vs RT markets; ancillary services; unit commitment vs economic dispatch; binding constraints

chapters.title: Practical Approximations
chapters.key: Continuous relaxation; exogenous flows; predictable battery dynamics; merit order dispatch; linearize losses

chapters.title: Types of Power Trades
chapters.key: DA/RT clearing; forwards/hedging; congestion/FTRs; spark spread; dark spread; effective heat rate; time spreads

ccgt_efficient.context: Homer City redevelopment target, very good

ccgt_typical.context: Standard combined cycle, most common spark spread reference

scgt.context: Simple cycle gas turbine, Brayton cycle only

coal_homer_city.context: Homer City's old coal units, uncompetitive vs 6-7 HR gas

peaker.context: Inefficient units including oil/diesel, dispatched last

homer_city.permit: PA DEP air quality approved Nov 2025

capacity_markets.mechanism: Periodic payment for generator existence (insurance against scarcity)
capacity_markets.caiso: Resource adequacy requirements — utilities negotiate with generators

energy_only.mechanism: No capacity payments; scarcity pricing provides investment signal
energy_only.ercot_mechanism: Price adder = VOLL × probability of lost load
energy_only.missing_money: Without scarcity pricing, marginal units earn zero profit and shut down

no_organized_market.mechanism: Regulated utilities with fixed cost-plus margin

pjm.coverage: PA, NJ, MD, VA, WV, OH, parts of IL, KY, MI, IN
pjm.key_feature: Most liquid US power market; Virginia is DC capital of US

caiso.key_feature: Renewables-forward, no coal; solar + wind + nuclear + gas only

ercot.key_feature: Isolated grid (third US interconnection); energy-only; legendary volatility
ercot.grid: Separate from Western and Eastern Interconnections; ~1 GW HVDC ties
ercot.wind: North and West Texas; drives price negative (to -$20/MWh); PTC subsidies keep turbines running
ercot.regulation: Not under FERC (due to grid isolation)
ercot.dc_bitcoin: Negative prices attracted Bitcoin mines, now data centers

miso.key_feature: Coal retirements → renewables; large wind; borders PJM with inter-regional flows
miso.coal_note: EIA May 2026: MISO coal units more profitable than gas recently
miso.dc_growth: Indiana, Illinois, Michigan popular for new DCs

nyiso.key_feature: Manhattan demand sink; upstate nuclear can't reach it (transmission constraint)

isone.key_feature: Winter gas scarcity forces oil dispatch

lmp.definition: Locational Marginal Price = Lagrange multiplier of each node's balance constraint
lmp.computation: Solved via Gurobi/CPLEX optimization of production cost model

spark_spread.formula: Power Price - (Heat Rate × Natural Gas Price)
spark_spread.example: 7 heat rate spark spread = Power - 7 × Gas
spark_spread.usage: Gas plant hedges by selling spark spread; trader buys if bullish on gas plant profitability

pricing_mechanics.dark_spread: Same as spark spread but for coal plants
pricing_mechanics.effective_heat_rate: Implied HR where gas plant earns $0 profit at current gas and power prices

hrco.name: Heat Rate Call Option
hrco.definition: Financial instrument mimicking plant economics; buyer gets upside, seller gets fixed payments
hrco.usage: Plant owner sells HRCO to lock in steady cash flows for debt underwriting

da_vs_rt.day_ahead: Computed day before delivery; most common market to trade; financial settlement
da_vs_rt.real_time: Recomputed every 5 minutes on delivery day; weather-driven
da_vs_rt.virtual_trading: Arbitrages DA vs RT price differences

ftr.name: Financial Transmission Rights
ftr.definition: Payoff depends on congestion between two nodes
ftr.usage: Basis trade — buy price at one location, sell at another

system_balance.general: Supply = Demand + Net Exports + Change in Storage
system_balance.power: Generation = Power Consumption + Net Power Exports + Change in Storage + Losses
constraints: Storage bounds (can't draw more than stored; max capacity)

duck_curve.definition: Net demand (demand minus renewables) very low daytime, high evening
duck_curve.cause: High solar/wind penetration depresses daytime prices to ~$0
duck_curve.consequence: Less efficient SCGTs needed in evening (cheap to start/stop); widens day-evening spread
duck_curve.solution: Batteries buy cheap daytime power, discharge in evening — flattening the curve

data_center_demand.note: Would outpace total US generation by mid-2030s at current doubling rate

grid_topology.ties: Limited HVDC between interconnections (~1 GW ERCOT-rest)
grid_topology.note: HVDC can connect grids at different frequencies but expensive to install

production_cost_model.output: Generation per unit + LMP at each node
production_cost_model.solver: Gurobi or CPLEX (mixed integer for unit commitment)
approximations: Predictable battery dynamics (charge day, discharge evening)
Merit order dispatch (sort by marginal cost)
production_cost_model.risks: Flow modeling errors; startup cost omission; no reliability constraints; demand model errors; BTM solar growth; new DC/BTC demand

energy_pipelines.what: Gas Chokepoint Dashboard — 36 LNG/gas equities, JKM-HH/TTF-HH spread betas
energy_pipelines.overlap: Henry Hub as reference gas price; international gas spread thesis
energy_pipelines.extension: Power 2026 shows how HH gas price flows through to power price via heat rate × gas price = variable cost of gas generation. The gas chokepoint thesis is UPSTREAM of the power thesis.

conditional_machine.what: BRIDGE v0.003 — natgas 53.8% annualized vol, 8-asset commodity universe
conditional_machine.extension: Gas plant is long a heat rate call option. Natgas vol directly impacts HRCO value and plant investment economics. The vol model feeds plant valuation.

portfolio_sleeve.what: Long Gas/Power sleeve: BE, ETN, SMR, VST (+6.6% delta, ~6% of portfolio variance)
portfolio_sleeve.extension: Power 2026 provides the fundamental WHY: capacity scarcity, interconnection queue, $329/MW-day PJM clearing, ERCOT energy-only volatility. These equities are plays on the primer's thesis.

gap_filled: No wholesale power market data existed — now have ISO structure, LMP mechanics, capacity auction data
No spark spread or heat rate framework — now have the gas→power price transmission mechanism
No interconnection/BTM data — now have queue analysis, Homer City case study, BTM compute framework
No production cost model — now have optimization framework, DA/RT markets, FTRs
